{{Short description|Message authentication code}}
{{Expand Russian|Two-Track-MAC|topic=sci|date=November 2016}}

'''Two-Track-MAC''' is a [[message authentication code]] submitted to the [[NESSIE]] project in 2000 by Bart Van Rompay (KU Leuven) and Bert den Boer (debis AG).<ref>{{cite report
 | last1 = Preneel
 | first1 = Bart
 | last2 = Van Rompay
 | first2 = Bart
 | last3 = Granboulan
 | first3 = Louis
 | last4 = Martinet
 | first4 = Guillaume
 | last5 = Murphy
 | first5 = Sean
 | last6 = Shipsey
 | first6 = Rachel
 | last7 = White
 | first7 = James
 | title = NESSIE Phase I: Selection of Primitives
 | institution = NESSIE Project
 | date = September 2001
 | url = https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Jean-Jacques-Quisquater/publication/2545150_NESSIE_Phase_I_Selection_of_primitives/links/02bfe510019956bb77000000/NESSIE-Phase-I-Selection-of-primitives.pdf
 | access-date = 2026-03-21
}}</ref>
It is based on a dual-track hashing structure derived from [[RIPEMD]], in which two [[parallel computing|parallel computation]] paths are combined to produce the final MAC.<ref name="two-track-mac">{{cite conference
 | last1 = den Boer
 | first1 = Bert
 | last2 = Van Rompay
 | first2 = Bart
 | last3 = Preneel
 | first3 = Bart
 | last4 = Vandewalle
 | first4 = Joos
 | chapter = New (two-track-) MAC based on the two trails of RIPEMD: Efficient, especially on short messages and for frequent key-changes
 | title = Selected Areas in Cryptography
 | series = Lecture Notes in Computer Science
 | volume = 2259
 | year = 2001
 | pages = 314–324
 | publisher = [[Springer Publishing]]
 | doi = 10.1007/3-540-45537-X_25
}}</ref>

It uses a dual-track structure derived from RIPEMD, in which two parallel computation paths are combined. This is superficially similar to constructions such as [[MDC-2]], which also employ parallel processing, though the underlying designs differ significantly.<ref name="two-track-mac"/>
